claims.statement: KSeF creates broad, recurring structured-invoice receipt volume in Poland from February 2026.
Official APIs and SDKs make a third-party integration technically possible, subject to customer-granted authorization and production security.
KSeF does not guarantee a bank account in every invoice because the relevant fields are optional.
NIP-account matching is public infrastructure with per-query confirmations and a daily bulk file, so it is not a proprietary data moat.
Basic whitelist verification is already embedded by major Polish ERP/accounting vendors.
Mandatory PSP payee verification will become another close substitute in non-euro Member States by July 2027.
Supplier account substitution is a demonstrated Polish business-fraud pattern for which independent confirmation is recommended.
A supplier-change approval record spanning KSeF, ERP history, and independent confirmation is a more differentiated wedge than account lookup alone.
No reviewed source establishes paid demand, achievable ARPU, channel commitment, false-positive rates, or retention for the proposed gate.

contrary_evidence: c702-s4 supplies the core public account match and bulk data at no license cost.
c702-s3 shows that the invoice may omit the account needed for a match.
c702-s7 and c702-s8 show incumbents already control adjacent workflow surfaces.
c702-s5 creates a bank-provided substitute on a fixed regulatory timetable.
